database: local synthetic copy of JMS staging (seed 7, cap 3000)

cases.question: Show me all active surrogates in Screening and list their current substage.
cases.title: Active surrogates in Screening and their sub-stages
cases.sql: SELECT g.case_id AS case_number, g.case_file_name AS case_name, st.status AS current_status, ts.title AS substage_name, cs.stage AS substage_workflow_stage, cs.ordering AS substage_order, CASE WHEN cs.completed IS NULL THEN 'Not completed' ELSE 'Completed' END AS completion_state, cs.completed AS completed_on FROM gc_case g JOIN custom_sub_stage cs ON cs.gc_case_id = g.case_id JOIN template_sub_stage ts ON ts.sub_stage_id = cs.base_sub_stage_id LEFT JOIN status st ON st.status_id = g.status_id WHERE g.active = 1 AND g.case_type = 'surrogate' AND g.stage = 'screening' ORDER BY g.case_file_name, cs.ordering
assumptions: 'Surrogate' means cases whose case type is surrogate (not donor or sperm donor).
'Active' means the case's active flag is set to 1.
'Screening' means the case's workflow stage is screening.

The case record has no single 'current substage' field, so the report lists every workflow sub-stage attached to each case, in order, with whether it is completed. Most sub-stages are not completed, so the current one is the first not-completed item in each case's list; this is a judgment call.
The current status column is the case's status label, shown for context.

cases.question: Which IP cases are in matching right now? Include the names and emails for both IPs.
cases.title: IP cases currently in the matching stage, with both IPs' names and emails
cases.sql:
SELECT ic.case_id AS case_number,
       ic.case_file_name AS case_name,
       ic.matching_type AS matching_type,
       CONCAT_WS(' ', c1.first_name, c1.last_name) AS ip_1_name,
       c1.email AS ip_1_email,
       CONCAT_WS(' ', c2.first_name, c2.last_name) AS ip_2_name,
       c2.email AS ip_2_email
FROM ip_case ic
LEFT JOIN family f ON f.family_id = ic.family_id
LEFT JOIN contact c1 ON c1.contact_id = f.ip_1_id
LEFT JOIN contact c2 ON c2.contact_id = f.ip_2_id
WHERE ic.stage = 'matching'
ORDER BY ic.case_id
assumptions: 'In matching' means the IP case's workflow stage is Matching (13 cases).
Both IPs are the two contacts linked to the case's family; the second IP is blank where the family has only one contact.
Email and name come from the contact record.

cases.question: List every active case assigned to [admin name].
Which cases have had their profiles approved in the last 30 days?
cases.title: Intended-parent cases with profiles approved in the last 30 days
cases.sql: SELECT i.case_id AS case_id, i.case_file_name AS case_name, f.family_id AS family_id, f.profile_approved AS profile_approved_on, i.stage AS case_stage, i.matching_type AS matching_type FROM family f JOIN ip_case i ON i.family_id = f.family_id WHERE f.profile_approved >= DATE_SUB('2026-10-21', INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND f.profile_approved < '2026-10-22' ORDER BY f.profile_approved DESC
assumptions: 'Cases' means intended-parent cases. Each one is linked to a family, and the approval is the family's profile approval date.
'Last 30 days' is 21 Sep 2026 through today (21 Oct 2026).

Only cases whose family profile was approved in that window are listed. Approvals on the contact-level profiles (egg donor, gestational carrier, sperm donor) have no approvals in that window, so they are not used here.

Two approved families in the window have no intended-parent case and therefore do not appear: family 62 (approved 21 Sep 2026) and family 34 (approved 15 Sep 2026 is outside the window, so only family 62 is affected).

cases.question: List egg donors available for a cycle who haven't donated before.
cases.title: Available egg donors who have never donated before
cases.sql: SELECT g.case_id AS case_number, g.case_file_name AS donor_name, g.donor_status AS donor_availability, g.stage AS case_stage, e.profile_id AS egg_donor_profile_id, CASE WHEN e.past_donor = 0 THEN 'No' ELSE 'Yes' END AS has_donated_before FROM gc_case g JOIN ed_profile e ON e.contact_id = g.gc_id WHERE g.case_type = 'donor' AND g.donor_status = 'available' AND e.past_donor = 0 ORDER BY g.case_file_name
assumptions: 'Available for a cycle' means the donor's case is marked as available (donor availability = available).
Only egg donor cases are included (case type 'donor'), not sperm donor or surrogate cases.
'Haven't donated before' means the donor profile is explicitly marked as not a past donor. Profiles where this is blank are excluded because it is unknown whether they donated.
Donors are matched to their egg donor profile through the contact linked to the case.

cases.question: Which contracts are still waiting on a signature?
cases.title: Signature requests still waiting on a signer
cases.sql: SELECT cr.relationship_id AS relationship_id, h.signature_request_id AS signature_request, CASE cr.status WHEN 'sent' THEN 'Sent, not opened' WHEN 'viewed' THEN 'Opened, not signed' WHEN 'undelivered' THEN 'Undelivered' ELSE cr.status END AS signature_status, cr.user_type AS signer_type, cr.user_id AS signer_id, cr.case_task_id AS case_task_id, DATE(cr.created) AS sent_on, DATE(h.created) AS request_created_on, CONCAT(a.first_name, ' ', a.last_name) AS created_by, DATE(cr.undelivered_email_at) AS undelivered_email_on, DATE(cr.undelivered_bell_at) AS undelivered_bell_on FROM contract_rel cr JOIN hellosign h ON h.hellosign_id = cr.parent_id LEFT JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = h.created_by_id WHERE cr.status IN ('sent','viewed','undelivered') ORDER BY cr.created
assumptions: Waiting on a signature means the signature request is sent, opened but not signed, or undelivered; signed requests are excluded.
Undelivered requests are included because the signer never received them, so they are still outstanding; they are labelled so you can filter them out.
Each row is one signer's request (one signature request can have several signers), so a single document may appear more than once.
Signer type shows whether the signer is a user, a non-platform user (np_user) or an admin.
Sent and request dates are shown as dates only.

cases.question: Show me which intended parents have never logged into their portal.
cases.title: Intended parents who have never logged in
cases.sql:
SELECT u.user_id AS `User ID`, u.first_name AS `First name`, u.last_name AS `Last name`, u.email AS `Email`, u.created AS `Account created`, u.confirmed_email AS `Email confirmed (1=yes)`, u.active AS `Active (1=yes)`
FROM `user` u
WHERE u.user_type = 'IP' AND u.last_login IS NULL
ORDER BY u.created DESC
assumptions: Intended parents are user accounts of type 'IP'; IP representatives are excluded.
Someone has never logged in if their account has no recorded last-login time.
Inactive accounts are included and flagged in the Active column.
Portal login is taken to be the same as the main account login, since no separate portal login record exists.

cases.question: Which cases have active, incomplete campaigns right now?
cases.title: Cases with active, incomplete campaigns
cases.sql: select g.case_id as case_id, g.case_file_name as case_name, g.case_type as case_type, g.stage as case_stage, c.internal_title as campaign, c.flow_status as campaign_flow_status, c.created as enrolled_on, c.flow_date as next_step_date from case_campaign c join gc_case g on g.case_id = c.assigned_gc_case where c.active = 1 and c.completed is null and (c.flow_status is null or c.flow_status not in ('finished','finished_by_trigger','stopped')) order by c.created desc
assumptions: 'Active' means the campaign enrollment is switched on and its flow is still running: starting, flowing or waiting. Flows that are finished, finished by trigger or stopped are excluded.
'Incomplete' means the enrollment has no completion date.
A case is linked to a campaign through the case assigned to that enrollment. Enrollments attached only to intended-parent cases, or with no case, are not listed.
The next step date is blank when no step is scheduled yet.

cases.question: Which surrogates are still waiting on their profile to be approved?
cases.title: Surrogates still waiting for profile approval
cases.sql: SELECT c.contact_id AS contact_id, CONCAT(c.first_name, ' ', c.last_name) AS surrogate_name, s.status AS current_status, s.stage AS current_stage, c.email AS email, c.phone_number AS phone, DATE(c.created) AS contact_created_date, c.sd_profile_approved AS sd_profile_approved FROM contact c JOIN status s ON s.status_id = c.status_id WHERE s.contact_type = 'surrogate' AND c.sd_profile_approved IS NULL ORDER BY c.created
assumptions: 'Surrogate' means contacts whose current status is a surrogate-type status (the status list marks these as 'surrogate'); 'SD' in this system appears to refer to surrogates.
'Still waiting on profile approval' means the surrogate profile approval date has never been set (empty).
Results cover all surrogate-type contacts, regardless of agency or assigned admin (all contacts belong to one agency).

cases.question: Show me egg donor profiles that haven't been approved by the agency yet.
cases.title: Egg donor profiles not yet approved by the agency
cases.sql: SELECT p.profile_id AS profile_id, p.contact_id AS contact_id, c.first_name AS first_name, c.last_name AS last_name, c.email AS email, c.phone_number AS phone_number, p.residency_status AS residency_status, p.race_1 AS primary_race, p.past_donor AS past_donor_flag, p.frozen_egg_count AS frozen_egg_count FROM ed_profile p LEFT JOIN contact c ON c.contact_id = p.contact_id WHERE c.ed_profile_approved IS NULL ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name, p.profile_id
assumptions: An egg donor profile counts as approved by the agency when its contact has an ED profile approval date recorded; profiles with no approval date are the ones shown.
Result: 276 of 280 egg donor profiles are not yet approved; only 4 have an approval date.
Each row is one profile, so a person with more than one profile appears more than once.

cases.question: Pull a list of sperm donors whose profiles are pending approval.
cases.title: Sperm donors with profiles pending IP approval
cases.sql: SELECT g.case_id AS sperm_donor_case_id, g.case_file_name AS donor_name, s.status AS current_status, g.stage AS workflow_stage, CASE WHEN g.active = 1 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS active_flag, DATE(g.created) AS created_date FROM gc_case g JOIN status s ON s.status_id = g.status_id WHERE g.case_type = 'sperm_donor' AND s.status = 'Pending IP Approval' ORDER BY g.created DESC
assumptions: 'Pending approval' means the current status is 'Pending IP Approval'.
Sperm donors are the sperm donor cases (case type sperm_donor).
The list includes both active and inactive cases; the active flag is shown so you can filter.
Other pending-type statuses (for example Pending Application, Pending Match, Pending Legal) were not counted as pending approval.

cases.question: Show me intended parents whose profile has been approved.
cases.title: Intended parents with approved profiles
cases.sql: SELECT ic.case_id AS case_number, ic.case_file_name AS case_name, ic.stage AS case_stage, CONCAT_WS(' ', c1.first_name, c1.last_name) AS primary_contact, CONCAT_WS(' ', c2.first_name, c2.last_name) AS second_contact, f.profile_approved AS profile_approved_on FROM ip_case ic JOIN family f ON f.family_id = ic.family_id LEFT JOIN contact c1 ON c1.contact_id = f.ip_1_id LEFT JOIN contact c2 ON c2.contact_id = f.ip_2_id WHERE f.profile_approved IS NOT NULL ORDER BY f.profile_approved DESC
assumptions: An intended parent's profile counts as approved when its family record has an approval date filled in.
Intended parents are the IP cases linked to those families; every IP case is included, whether active or not.
Contact names come from the family's first and second contacts.
